notes.title: Field Notes: Week 7 – Sunday
notes.notes:
They came at night…

Those things... The way they moved, the way they screeched—it was like the forest itself had birthed them, shaped them to hunt us.

I understand now. We were never going to make it back from the 5th. The forest knew. It always knew. It was waiting.

Everyone’s gone. Anton, Louis... all of them. Bullets were useless.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/0e9ac39c97238815774c721409fe359efcd33473.jpg[/img]

I’m the only one left. I can hear them—scratch, scratch, scratching at the door. It won’t hold much longer.

Still have a few grenades. Maybe I can rig this place to blow, take these freaks with me.

Stranger, if you find this, you have to get back to the Arc. Warn them about what’s coming. There’s no more time!

notes.title: Field Notes: Week 6 – Deep Recon
notes.notes:
Rumors are going around. Something’s going on in the 5th arrondissement. What exactly, we aren’t sure. 

We captured a raconteur—barely more than a scavenger with a knife and a bad sense of timing. Under some “encouragement,” he told us the cultists are moving. Entire groups heading toward the 5th, chanting their prayers to the forest.

Whatever’s going on, we need to know. 

And I drew the short straw, along with Anton and Louis. The task is simple, get there and report back anything that seems significant. 

The first few days were uneventful, but as we press deeper, things are getting…stranger. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/3bc8be0cef2920dd62d766ab970c4a067e7e2d44.jpg[/img]

By the fourth day, we started noticing changes. The trees seem different, taller and more twisted.
And then there’s the shadows.

I thought I was psyching myself out. But Anton saw them too. Flickers of movement at the edge of our vision. Yet when we stopped to investigate, there was nothing.  No tracks, no nothing. 
We found them on the fifth day. It was Louis who spotted the bodies first. Five cultists, sprawled in a loose circle near the remains of an old fountain. Their garments were torn and filthy, their faces frozen in terror. Whatever did this, I hope we don’t run into it. 

We made camp in an apartment block nearby. 
That’s when the dreams started. Dreams that seem to pull me toward something.

notes.title: Field Notes: Week 5 – Marauders
notes.notes:
Patrolling solo is always a bad idea, but sometimes there’s no choice if we want to get enough coverage. I was near the Jardin des Plantes, keeping a low profile, when I heard them—voices, low and gruff.

Raconteurs.

I ducked into the undergrowth, gripping my rifle tight as I peeked through the leaves. There were four of them, armed with crude weapons: pipes, machetes, an old hunting rifle. They were laughing, passing around a bottle of something.

They must’ve known I was there because as soon as I moved to slip away, one of them yelled, “Come out, mon ami! We just wanna talk.”

I bolted.

I made it maybe 15 yards before I stumbled into a dead end—a wall of gnarled roots rising too high to climb. I turned, rifle up, just as the first marauder burst through the brush. He grinned, teeth yellow and jagged, and raised his machete.

“Nowhere to run,” he said, his buddies closing in behind him.

He wasn’t wrong. My back was to the wall, my ammo low, and four against one wasn’t a fight I’d win. Not with bullets, anyway. But then I looked up.

Hanging in the branches above us were clusters of seeds I’d never seen before, gleaming faintly in the dim light. I recalled what had happened to Gabriel.

Out of time and out of ideas, I raised my rifle and fired, aiming high. The shot rang out, and the seeds fell, their pods snapping open mid-air. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/f61b00686cb24b014414082215139c5be77b7da1.jpg[/img]

The raconteurs never knew what hit them.

The seeds darted toward them, buzzing like angry hornets. One exploded on impact, tearing the leader apart. Another chased the man with the rifle, detonating just as he turned to run.

The last two tried to scatter, but the seeds were relentless. One exploded at the edge of the clearing, and the final marauder—the bastard—ran straight for me, hoping to use me as a shield. The last seed caught him just a few feet away, the blast knocking me flat on my back.

When the smoke cleared, I was the only one left standing.

These seeds saved my life, but they don’t discriminate. My coat is shredded, and I’ve got a gash on my leg. It could’ve been worse. Should’ve been worse.

As I limped back to the Arc, I couldn’t shake the image of the seeds chasing those men, like the forest itself wanted them gone.

Maybe it did.

notes.title: Field Notes: Week 4 – Cultists
notes.notes:
I’m more and more grateful I made it to the Arc. It offers some semblance of life, community. Without that, people get strange…

We were on patrol when we saw them—a small group of three, barely more than silhouettes in the mist. They moved like they’d been out here a while, shoulders hunched, cautious but purposeful.
I approached, hands up, keeping my rifle slung. Anton hung back, covering me.
I told them we were from the Arc, that we had shelter and medicine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/470724121ee015e907f876458b24b8a1744daa6a.jpg[/img]

They turned to face us, their faces obscured by masks carved from wood or bone.

“We’re fine where we are,” the leader said. A woman, maybe? Her voice was low, calm. “The forest provides.”

I told them they were crazy, that they were going to die out here. But they couldn’t be convinced. 

That night on the Arc, we heard singing. Low and guttural, like a chant, echoing through the forest. Nobody slept.

notes.title: Field Notes: Week 3 – Finding Supplies
notes.notes:
Life at the Arc is better than I thought it would be. The engineers have outdone themselves, rigging up a pulley system to move supplies—and people—to the top. It’s crude, loud, and far from perfect, but it works. 

The word must be spreading, because every day brings new survivors. We’ve gone from a handful of weary stragglers to something resembling a community. More hands to work, sure, but also more mouths to feed. That’s the trade-off: growth means risk, and risk means patrols.

We’ve been combing the city, scavenging anything we can. Food, medicine, even just tools or scrap metal—it all has value. Most places have long since been picked clean, but if you’re willing to go deeper into the city, you can still find a few things. If you survive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/62fe51e5ee0b451236bd7aa8b8b1ab727551c6a6.jpg[/img]

Yesterday, we hit a block near Rue Coquillière. We checked an old boulangerie. The upstairs was barren—empty shelves, shattered glass, dust thick enough to choke on. But in the basement, we found…
A rat swarm was eating a corpse.

Hearing us come down, the rats turned. Their eyes glinted, their bodies shuddered, and then one of them… popped.

The explosion was small but vicious, sending a spray of spores and viscera across the room. We fired, retreating up the stairs as more rats began to swell and burst. The noise was deafening, the stench unbearable, but we managed to fight our way out. 

Once we were safe, I looked back. The rats were dead, but the spores lingered in the air like a malevolent fog.

notes.title: Field Notes: Week 2 – Hunting
notes.notes:
They sent me out on hunting detail with Gabriel and Anton—two guys I barely know, but out here, trust is a luxury we can’t wait to build. We broke camp at first light and headed north in search of boar. They’re easy to track, noisy and destructive, and travel in packs.

By mid-morning, we found them. A small group rooting around near the Galeries Lafayette, their tusks scraping against the cracked stone. Their skin had a strange sheen to it, and some of them had moss growing along their backs. 

Everything here changes, even the animals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/f04eb423216036252df02d77dccebb0a88de1d28.jpg[/img]

Gabriel volunteered to take the shot. He crouched low, moving silently through the long grass. Anton and I hung back to keep watch. The forest seemed calm for a moment—no snapping branches, no distant howls. Just the rustle of wind through the grass.

Then Gabriel fired.

The boar scattered, squealing, but something else happened, too. The grass he was crouching in… moved. Not with the wind, but with purpose. It stiffened into a thousand little razors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/03178a7f2cdbd3c75ce3da7d125505d8a14b9e18.jpg[/img]

Gabriel didn’t even have time to scream.

When it was over, the grass…relaxed…I guess it is the word, swaying gently as if nothing had happened. Gabriel was gone, shredded, his blood soaking into the earth.

I’ve never seen the forest do that before.

We stood there for what felt like hours, staring at the spot where Gabriel had been. Eventually, Anton snapped out of it, muttering something about finishing the job. We tied up the boar Gabriel shot and started dragging it back to camp.

The forest doesn’t just kill. It punishes.

We got our boar. But we’re down a man.

notes.title: Field Notes: Week 1 – Arrival
notes.notes:
[i]*These are recovered field notes found on the Citizens base. Unnamed survivor describes his exploration of the new world. No records on his personality have been ever found. You now have access to these papers, as they may drastically increase your chances for survival in the Forest.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/1d610c595f8f822263f6d221232a7d87e41412fb.jpg[/img]

I made it. Somehow, against all odds, I made it.

By the time I reached the Arc, I was exhausted, starving, and more than a little afraid. But the rumors were true: survivors are here. It’s not much yet, just some tents and makeshift barricades, but it’s something.

A few of the newcomers have engineering experience, and they’re already talking about building a pulley system to haul supplies—and people—up to the top of the Arc. A crazy idea, but with the way the forest is at night, crazy might just keep us alive.

It’s strange, being around people again. Sharing a fire, trading stories, even arguing over what to do next. It feels fragile, like one bad night could tear it all apart.

But there’s strength in numbers. Maybe, just maybe, we can build something here. Something worth holding onto.

notes.title: Take a Deep Dive into Forest Reigns FPS
notes.notes:
VG Entertainment has released an in-depth gameplay showcase for Forest Reigns, a new story-driven FPS set in post-apocalyptic Paris. 

The nearly 8-minute video highlights three distinct ways to approach a single mission, emphasizing player’s freedom of choice and the environmental interactions. The Forest is not just a backdrop, it's an intelligence you can either fight against or turn into an ally.

[list]
[*] [b]Direct assault. Antagonizing the Forest:[/b] Fight alongside a squad, use firepower, and manipulate the hostile environment to your advantage.
[*][b] Stealth attack. At one with the Forest:[/b] Strike from the shadows, use nature as a tool, and turn enemies against each other.
[*] [b]Exploration approach. Withstand the Forest:[/b] Discover hidden paths, turn environmental traps to your advantage, and use the city’s remnants to outsmart foes.
[/list]

Forest Reigns offers deep and emergent gameplay where every choice shapes the experience and the whole story. Watch the full deep-dive video on our page on Steam and wishlist!

notes.title: Forest Reigns FAQ: Your Questions Answered
notes.notes:
Curious about Forest Reigns? Wondering if it’s open-world, coming to consoles, single-player only, or has multiple endings? While our team is getting ready with a new deep dive video, we’ve answered some of these frequently asked questions in comments, social media posts, and interviews and are bringing everything together here for your convenience.

Feel free to reach out on social media if you don’t find what you’re looking for. We’re always happy to chat! :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/cb4cc8f6418a2485c4030e02ece7a0636271748c.jpg[/img]

[h3]1. What inspired Forest Reigns?[/h3]
Our passion has always been crafting story-driven single-player experiences, and Forest Reigns is a return to that vision. With this game, we aim to deliver a thrilling, visually stunning and engaging adventure.

We’ve always been fascinated by interactive environments, and our past projects included elements of that. With Forest Reigns, we wanted to take it further. Here, the forest is not just a setting. It’s something you can interact with, adapt to, and have fun with in combat.

[h3]2. Why Paris?[/h3]
Paris offers a rich historical and cultural backdrop, making it an exciting setting for exploration and survival. Its unique architecture combined with the contrast between urban landscapes and the overgrown nature was the main reason for choosing it.

Also, Paris is a popular tourist destination, so many players who’ve been to the City of Light will recognize and compare the real places to our artistic interpretations. It’s pretty fascinating when you’re playing a video game and suddenly think: “Hey, I’ve been there!”

[h3]3. How does the forest shape gameplay?[/h3]
The Forest is the central part of the game, its key character. It’s alive and intelligent, so the entire ecosystem responds to players’ actions.

If you trigger its aggression and lure enraged creatures toward your enemies, nature might do the fighting for you. But be careful: once the forest enters its aggressive state, you might become its next target!

[h3]4. Can players manipulate the forest?[/h3]
Yes! Early in the game, harm will be one of the main triggers causing the Forest to respond. 
Over time, players will unlock other methods: consumables, equipment choices, and decisions made during missions, and all of these can influence how the Forest reacts to humans and the player.

[h3]5. Where do mutated animals and plants come from?[/h3]
Animals are an integral part of the Forest and they are imbued by it. If humans disrupt or harm the forest, it reacts, and the transformation of creatures is part of that response. 
We’ll reveal more about the flora and fauna as development continues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/2c41334eda51bbe1b01804059eda922337ecde7d.jpg[/img]

[h3]6. Are there factions? Can we join them? What are their names?[/h3]
Absolutely! As mentioned in our announcement, Forest Reigns features multiple factions, each with a distinct vision for the future of humanity.

Their perspectives will revolve around their relationship with nature and other survivors. Your alliances with some of them will shape the story, granting access to resources, technology, and unique benefits.

We don’t reveal the names so far, cause we want you to discover them as you play. :)

[h3]7. Will we play a predefined character? [/h3]
Yes, the protagonist has a set identity and backstory, deeply tied to the main narrative. However, your choices will shape the journey, relationships, and the final of the story.

[h3]8. How long will the game be?[/h3]
We're not revealing all the details yet, but you can expect a few dozen hours of survival in the green apocalypse in Paris.
Considering the freedom to explore the world, the only limit here is how much time and effort you’re willing to spend uncovering every corner of the city.

[h3]9. How large is the map? Can we explore it entirely as an open world?[/h3]
We’re not focused on the size of the map, but rather on creating a world that’s interesting to explore, where quality is over quantity. Details about the map will come later.

As for accessibility, almost the entire map will be open for exploration, except for a few story-restricted areas. However, some regions will require players to have better equipment.

[h3]10. Are there missions, side quests, survival, and RPG elements?[/h3]
In terms of structure, it’s more classic for an RPG than for a shooter. There’s the main storyline and a large number of side missions. 
The player can choose what to do and in what order to do it.

There will be free exploration, a perk system, side quests, and a branching storyline with multiple endings. Survival is also one of the key features: crafting, resource gathering, and strategic planning always matter. Players will need to manage gear, repair weapons, and adapt to various in-game situations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/51ed4a6047c515faf14c72de998a82dba522f10a.jpg[/img]

[h3]11. What unique mechanics stand out?[/h3]
Expect the unexpected! The interactive forest is our core feature – an intelligent, reactive environment that responds to your every move. Nature is your ally, your enemy, and a mystery to uncover.

[h3]12. Can we stealth through the whole game?[/h3]
You’ll be able to use stealth if that’s your preferred approach, but relying solely on stealth to complete all the missions will be nearly impossible. 

The best strategy is to mix different play styles, and we design missions to ensure varied gameplay. We don’t want to create another straightforward and linear game where you use only one style, repeat the same actions, and eventually get bored after just a few missions.

Soon we’ll share a deep dive video that will reveal different playthrough scenarios, but these are not the only options though.

[h3]13. How realistic is the shooting?[/h3]
Gunplay is grounded, with attention to accuracy, recoil, and ammo management. But in Forest Reigns, survival matters just as much. Combat isn’t just about pulling the trigger. It’s about using the environment to stay alive.

[h3]14. Can we customize and upgrade weapons?[/h3]
Yes! Weapons and gear will be fully customizable. You can upgrade them with the necessary materials or improvements you find. But be careful, gear deteriorates with every fight, so you’ll also need to repair it.

[h3]15. How does crafting work?[/h3]
You’ll be able to craft weapons, medical supplies, and other items (which we’ll reveal later), as well as repair or upgrade your gear. 

Materials can be gathered through purchases or looting, and special crafting stations will be used to transform these into useful things.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/be49997554a111ed3269a80ba8ac773d8dbeebdf.jpg[/img]

[h3]16. How deep are survival mechanics? Hunger, thirst, base-building?[/h3]
Though there won’t be anything like hunger and thirst, resources will be scarce, and survival will require constant scavenging. Crafting is a key part of survival too. You’ll be able to craft weapons, medical supplies, and other useful items, as well as repair and upgrade your gear to avoid unexpected breakdowns. 

Base-building isn’t part of the plan, but players will have access to faction settlements if they manage to keep good relationships with them.

[h3]17. Will there be a co-op mode?[/h3]
Right now, we focus solely on creating a high-quality single-player FPS. We want to deliver an immersive, story-driven experience first and see how we could evolve it in the future, based on the players' preferences. Co-op playthrough could be one of such options.

[h3]18. What’s the focus of the graphics?[/h3]
We use a "stylized realism" approach, balancing detailed environments with a slightly fictional touch for a unique, immersive world. 

This approach is a deliberate artistic choice that shapes the vibe of the world. For example, just like in Dishonored, a world that is stylized yet gains a unique charm because of it.

[h3]19. What emotions do you want players to feel?[/h3]
We hope players will think something like: "Wow, this is both impressive and fun!", however, completing missions flawlessly won’t always be easy. Adapting to the forest, using well-planned tactics, and making the most of traps and natural elements will be key to survival.

Beyond entertainment, we aim to spark thought-provoking discussions about science, ecology, and humanity’s relationship with nature. By experiencing the tension between civilization and nature, players may walk away with a deeper connection to nature and their awareness of its fragility.

[h3]20. Will there be French and Ukrainian voice-overs?[/h3]
We currently have a preliminary set of languages on Steam. We're working on adding French and Ukrainian voice-overs, and even more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/79eea54a2e89aab741ea6415a255baad83372e3b.jpg[/img]

[h3]21. Any plans for a collector’s edition?[/h3]
That could be a good idea! We'll consider what makes sense in that regard closer to the release time. For the moment, we are fully focused on the game development.

[h3]22. Which platforms will it be on?[/h3]
The game will also be released on PS 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

[h3]23. Which engine are you using?[/h3]
We’re developing Forest Reigns on Unreal Engine 5 for a high-quality, immersive experience. 

[h3]24. When’s the release date?[/h3]
We don’t have a release date yet. We’re focused on quality first, and the development of the fascinating world for you to explore is our #1 priority.
Once we decide on a certain date, we’ll announce it on Steam, our website, and social media when we’re ready. Stay tuned!

[h3]25. Where can players stay updated on Forest Reigns?[/h3]
We’ll be sharing all our updates through our official media channels. Kindly find links to our social media pages and a newsletter subscription form here on the official website. 

Also, we’ll share the news on our Steam page. All new videos will be published on the [url=https://www.youtube.com/@forestreigns]Forest Reigns YouTube channel[/url], so stay tuned for our new deep dive one, it’s coming soon! ;)

notes.title: Remembering Viktor Antonov, our dear friend
notes.notes:
All our team is deeply sad that our friend Viktor Antonov, has passed away. He was the visionary art director of Forest Reigns and helped us shape its unique style. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/153025991ed7b7c8ef1fe6f34be7bb6a98f89eae.jpg[/img]

Viktor's creative drive helped us break free from the limited post-Soviet way of seeing the world. He taught us to approach world-building with more artistry and imagination. His ideas were and will still be a huge part of the game. 

Though the loss is immense, Viktor’s creativity will live on in the worlds he helped create. And we’ll do our best to keep his style and vision alive in Forest Reigns.

notes.title: Forest Reigns in the Spotlight
notes.notes:
Our new project has caught the eye of media outlets with its intriguing concept. Here’s what early impressions from the media have to say about our title:

[i]“Forest Reigns, a post-apocalyptic tale set in the heart of a devastated yet floral Paris, could be a game that unlocks more potential for an FPS genre that’s crying out for new directions.
It could be one of the most unique FPS games on our radar right now.” [/i]– Forbes

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/c0870002e3dc890d4853beff6ac7b0723eadcaa0.jpg[/img]

[i]“We just got the first trailer for one of the most fascinating-looking games of 2025, and it’s already giving me strong Far Cry and The Last of Us vibes. Regardless of what you can draw comparisons to however, it looks absolutely beautiful.” [/i]– Gaming Bible

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/c1ced165948aaa4011231e2f2602cb92388b936e.jpg[/img]

[i]“The encroaching forest is alive, and you'll see how the iconic sights of Paris have been reshaped by an aggressive Mother Nature. 
Survival crafting, a non-linear story, and a forest that can serve as both friend and foe in any given situation all combine to try and set Forest Reigns apart.” [/i]– IGN

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/53de0ef92939a6ebcffb057c32e8758bc3b0d9c5.jpg[/img]

[i]“Unlike the usual post-apocalyptic greyed-out visuals, Forest Reigns contrasts the fall of Paris with a bright and mystical palette reminiscent of Outer Worlds.
The reveal trailer and Steam page showcase unique mechanics, including the ability to use the forest's disdain for humanity to your advantage when facing other human enemies.” [/i]– DualShockers

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/6428997133b3d18b3bbf6eda9b52ff40e8e85ab4.jpg[/img]

[i]“As a fan of weird forests, which is to say all forests, I'm keen on the prospect of an FPS set in a post-apocalyptic Paris that has been overrun by sentient, pissed-off trees. 
It's from a team led by a former S.T.A.L.K.E.R. developer, too, and those S.T.A.L.K.E.R. alumni certainly know how to post a good apocalypse.” [/i]– Rock Paper Shotgun

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/d8788d35db5ab6f213e9753320596a473b602764.jpg[/img]

[i]“In a market filled with post-apocalyptic shooters, Forest Reigns sets itself apart by flipping the script. It trades barren wastelands for lush forests, and mindless enemies for a thinking, reactive ecosystem. With its emergent gameplay, a gripping non-linear story, and a stunning reimagining of Paris, the game challenges players to rethink survival and combat in a world where nature has taken over.” [/i]– Early Game

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/d3cd3ac37d44888bd8270096695a6d9a5e061430.jpg[/img]

[i]“The developers promise not only an exciting “sandbox” but also an interesting narrative component. It sounds very much like S.T.A.L.K.E.R., but the game is obviously not as gloomy, more vibrant, and some scenes even seem fantastical.”[/i] – ITC

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/d42c4f1fdd431589b22940b90957b74ca1db7ff2.jpg[/img]

[i]“Forest Reigns looks like a beautiful blend of gameplay with elements of Stalker, Crysis and Fallout wrapped up in a neat package. This sounds like everything I want in a modern single-player FPS.” [/i]– Gaming on Linux

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/83d73fd7cc20aa605dbff1715d00c8bbf3f9d123.jpg[/img]

[i]“Forest Reigns is like taking a healthy dose of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and mixing with it some Annihilation for good measure. The visuals seem oddly colorful, with all manners of exotic tree life dousing the city in various hues.
Resources will be scarce. You must plan, scavenge, and craft to survive.” [/i]– Notebookcheck

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/f07e3a3da94d92e58ef6b3821a5d6a72b301f578.jpg[/img]

[i]“With its ambitious art direction, Forest Reigns features mechanisms where nature reacts to players' actions. From the Arc de Triomphe invaded by intelligent plants to the Ministry of the Environment, each location promises unique challenges.”[/i] – Sortir à Paris

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438345/e60962a6e8a9846349fe90543977c94e7c7ac063.jpg[/img]

With our revamped approach to post-apocalyptic storytelling and gameplay, Forest Reigns is also beginning to draw players' attention. If you’re searching for an FPS that offers something fresh, this might just be the game to surprise you.

Wishlist to be the first to play it!
